Diagnostic analytics

Why did it happen?

Find the pressure points: compare revenue with costs, inspect Week 12 branches and dayparts, and challenge possible explanations. Observed clues do not establish causes.

CLUE 01 / NETWORK

More traffic did not pay the bills.

Recorded entries · W1 → W12+71.4%
Completed orders · W1 → W12+11.1%
Net revenue increase+₱32.3k
Food + other operating cost increase+₱82k
The cost increase exceeds net revenue growth by ₱49.7k, exactly the operating profit deterioration. Discounts rose from 5.6% to 14.1% of gross sales; wait rose from 8 to 24 minutes.

Exhibit 1 · W1 vs W12. Entries +1,500; orders +140; costs 171 → 253.

CLUE 02 / WEEK 12 SNAPSHOT

South Quad is the service warning.

Orders ÷ recorded entries · not customer conversion

Week 12 branch profit: North −₱11.2k, Library −₱10.1k, South −₱13.4k. South also logs 9 stockouts versus North’s 4. Branch wait samples are clues from different windows.

Exhibit 2 · Peak = 11:30–13:30 + 17:30–19:30. Dayparts partition branch totals; do not add them again.

Rival explanation, survey evidence and what would distinguish causes

Rival explanation: crowd composition changed.

Re-entry, voucher-driven visits or a campus event could raise counter entries without comparable buying demand. Queue friction and stockouts could also suppress completed orders. The campaign changed midway; these uncontrolled trends do not isolate an effect.

Distinguishing evidence: aligned 15-minute entries, queue joins/abandons, completions, promotions, menu availability and staffing, plus a campus event calendar. Compare matched time windows in a safeguarded staggered pilot; do not infer missing sales from stockout counts.

Survey: a signal, not a causal estimate

Short wait return intention = 42/60 = 70%
Over 20 min return intention = 16/50 = 32%
Difference = 38 percentage points

Convenience sample: 180 volunteers. Wait is self-reported; intention is not observed repurchase. No person-level or POS links exist. The association supports testing service improvements, but cannot quantify orders recovered.

FINAL BOARD RECOMMENDATION / BULLETIN 01

A alone: express pickup, with cash access protected.

Choose A at ₱18k setup and +₱6k four-week planning impact. Compare with the retained A+C package: ₱26k setup and −₱5k impact under the updated rules. A saves ₱8k upfront and delivers ₱11k more four-week benefit. C alone now returns −₱4k versus its earlier +₱12k; its cheaper setup no longer offsets the weaker estimate.

Trade-off: A risks ₱18k of setup capital if uplift fails and needs counter space. Do nothing has zero setup cost and zero incremental improvement. A’s possible wait reduction is unverified. Keep an assisted cash route and the existing budget meal. A has the highest planning benefit among all feasible supplied packages and meets the positive-benefit planning objective: +₱6k after setup within the ₱27k cap. Actual results and access safeguards must be checked during Weeks 13–16.

REVIEW RULE / OPERATIONS

Reduce loss without hiding service strain.

Operations measures mean end-to-end wait using consistent weekday and time windows. Operational success: a comparable network mean of ≤24 minutes each pilot week. Stop/review: any week above 24 minutes. Finance separately measures cumulative incremental operating profit after setup against a consistent no-pilot comparison: success is >₱0 by Week 16. Review at Week 14 if incremental operating benefit before setup is ≤0. These are proposed rules, not observed pilot results.

REVIEW RULE / INCLUSION

Keep the door open to every student.

Log denied cash transactions and availability of the existing budget meal at lunch/dinner. Establish availability baseline before launch. Success: zero cash denials and budget-meal availability at least at baseline every pilot week. Pause immediately: any forced digital-only payment or removal of the existing budget meal. Staff consent and no involuntary overtime are launch conditions for every package.

Trust & sources · data judgment and actual AI audit

Trust the arithmetic. Question the story.

Sources, assumptions and actual AI use
DATA JUDGMENT / CHAPTERS 1–2

What the source can support

Five structured CSV tables + narrative PDF

Weekly network ledger: 12 time-series rows. Branch and daypart tables: Week 12 cross-sections and partitions. Survey: three aggregated category-count rows, 180 volunteers. Intervention menu: five prospective estimates. PDF supplies definitions, context and rules.

Two measurement cautions

1. Entries permit re-entry; transactions permit repeat buyers. Therefore orders/entry measures transactions relative to counter observations, not unique-customer conversion.
2. Branch waits use different windows without aligned weights. Therefore they cannot be averaged to recover the network’s 24-minute mean or used as a precise ranking of comparable waits.

Source conflicts reconciled

Week 10: use Finance’s ₱28.5k total discounts; Marketing’s ₱26k public vouchers is a subset (₱2.5k scope difference). Using Marketing alone would overstate profit by ₱2.5k.
Week 11: use 1,440 reconciled orders = 1,470 early export − 30 voids. Using 1,470 would raise both moving-average predictions by 10 orders.

Useful missing dataset

An aligned queue-to-order log by branch/time, with staffing, promotion, stock availability, cash denials and budget-meal availability. It would separate demand from service friction and establish access baselines. There is no actual repurchase or cash-access history to claim.

Sources: supplied README; Exhibits 1–4; student PDF pp.2–4. No external observations added.

ACTUAL AI AUDIT / CHAPTERS 3–6

A proposal challenged, then updated with the bulletin.

These are excerpts from the actual pre-bulletin analytical exchange used while building this dashboard, not simulated chat records. Their original estimates are retained as history, not current recommendations.

Actual analytical prompt · excerpt

“Recommend an initial feasible four-week pilot under the PHP35k budget using page 4's lower-bound single-option and 75%-of-summed-lower-bound combination rules. Explain the trade-off between cash impact and queue relief”

Initial AI proposal: A+C: ₱26k setup, ₱8.25k weekly uplift, +₱7k four-week impact. Before the bulletin, C alone was the stronger four-week financial option.

Actual follow-up · excerpt

“Your A+C proposal costs PHP26k and produces +PHP7k over four weeks, while C alone costs PHP8k and produces +PHP12k. Why spend PHP18k more for PHP5k less incremental impact? Does the evidence establish that reducing waits will recover orders, and does A+C make the operator profitable?”

Independent numerical check · local Python Decimal

PRE-BULLETIN CHECK
C: 4 × 5 − 8 = +12k
A+C: 4 × [0.75 × (6 + 5)] − 26 = +7k
C advantage: +5k; upfront cash saved: 18k

POST-BULLETIN CHECK
A: 4 × 6 − 18 = +6k
A+C: 4 × [0.75 × (6 + 1)] − 26 = −5k
C: 4 × 1 − 8 = −4k
Initial A+C change: −5 − 7 = −12k
A ongoing: −34.7 + 6 = −28.7k/week

Verified directly from the original and bulletin CSV inputs using deterministic Decimal arithmetic. All 32 option subsets were checked against the ₱27k cap: A alone has the largest feasible planning impact, +₱6k. Branch totals, daypart partitions and the unchanged forecast also reconcile.

Refinement: the follow-up changed the pre-bulletin working choice from A+C to C. The actual bulletin then reduced C’s estimate, so the final recommendation changes to A alone, compared with feasible A+C. Retain the initial A+C record, the 75% overlap rule and all access safeguards. A meets the planning objective of positive four-week incremental profit within budget. Ongoing operations still lose money; actual improvement and inclusion safeguards require pilot measurement.

Check script + machine-readable result included in the export. Another AI’s agreement was not used as numerical verification.
